2607.29334.title: The persuasive power of large language models does not depend on their perceived national origin
2607.29334.paper_summary: Conversational AI developed by geopolitical rivals reaches citizens worldwide, raising concerns that it could sway public opinion or be rejected as foreign propaganda, with consequences for democratic discourse and information sovereignty. Yet, whether an AI's perceived national origin shapes its persuasive power is unknown. In a preregistered randomized experiment, 403 adults from a nationally representative United States sample held a three-round debate with a chatbot introduced as either American ("DiscoveryAI") or Chinese ("ZhengheAI"), discussing a political or non-political topic. In all conditions, participants actually conversed with the same model (GPT-4o), instructed to argue against their initial position. We combined pre- and post-conversation self-reports of attitudes, trust, and collective narcissism with computational analyses of 1,209 participant turns, including LLM-coded stance and argumentative conduct, stance-sensitive embeddings, and keyword-masked emotion and toxicity classifiers. The conversations produced substantial attitude changes in every condition. Critically, the nationality label affected neither self-reported attitude change nor expressed stance, concessions, counterarguing, or affect, and equivalence tests and Bayes factors largely supported these null effects. The label's only reliable footprint was lower pre-conversation human-like trust in the Chinese model, whereas functionality trust was unaffected. Political topics slowed stance movement toward the AI's position, and collective narcissism predicted less attitude change regardless of origin, acting as a general barrier rather than an out-group filter. Users thus initially withhold social trust from a rival's AI yet still assimilate its arguments; origin labeling and transparency requirements alone may offer weak protection against foreign influence operations conducted through conversational AI.
2607.29334.paper_summary_zh: 地緣政治對手開發的對話式人工智慧遍及全球公民，引發了人們的擔憂，認為它可能影響公共意見或被拒絕為外國宣傳，對民主話語和資訊主權造成後果。然而，AI的國家來源是否影響其說服力仍然未知。在一項預註冊的隨機實驗中，來自全國代表性美國樣本的403名成年人與一個被介紹為美國（“DiscoveryAI”）或中國（“ZhengheAI”）的聊天機器人進行了三輪辯論，討論政治或非政治主題。在所有條件下，參與者實際上與相同的模型（GPT-4o）對話，該模型被指示反駁他們的初始立場。我們結合了對話前後的自我報告態度、信任和集體自戀，並進行了對1,209名參與者的回合進行計算分析，包括LLM編碼的立場和論證行為、立場敏感的嵌入以及關鍵詞屏蔽的情感和毒性分類器。這些對話在每個條件下都產生了顯著的態度變化。關鍵的是，國籍標籤既未影響自我報告的態度變化，也未影響表達的立場、讓步、反駁或情感，等效性測試和貝葉斯因子在很大程度上支持了這些無效效果。該標籤唯一可靠的跡象是在與中國模型的對話前，對人類般的信任較低，而功能性信任則未受影響。政治主題減緩了立場向AI立場的移動，而集體自戀預測了無論來源如何的態度變化較少，這充當了一個普遍的障礙，而不是一個外群體過濾器。因此，使用者最初對對手的AI保留社會信任，但仍然吸收其論點；僅靠來源標籤和透明度要求可能對通過對話式AI進行的外國影響行動提供微弱的保護。
